en: He wore arranged in nine styles.
The shawm set his army moving,
The many Kytay swarmed forward,
War drums deafening the ears,
Driving chosen giants from Beejin,
Driving all their champions together.
The sky was clear, the earth overcast;
Flying soil became a cloud of dust.
Ezkara of the Manchus,
He was the judge of warriors;
Champion Zholoy was beside him.
Onto the rough, hilly neck of land,
Ezkara now emerged
And turned Chongküröng's head.
At the wrathful, bloodstained gray-maned hero,
Ezkara stood gazing.
Ezkara among the unbelievers
Was an outstanding seer, his vision open;
A judge of warriors, deeply knowing,
Whose name frightened those who heard it.
The spells of wondrous lore
He recited unlike other men.
Do not ask about that accursed one:
A surpassing seer and sorcerer,
He was an extraordinary warrior.
Straining like one whose husband had died,
The mighty, bloodstained Manas—
It was his form he now beheld.
Seeing that form, Ezkara
Began to lose his senses.
From atop Chongküröng,
Ezkara, who had been acting so grand,
Nearly fell to the ground.
As though about to die,
He drew his throat tight.
“Oh, dear Zholoy, come here;
Did you see what I saw?
That man riding across on the spotted horse,
With an unsheathed sword strapped on,
Like a cloud about to rain again,
Wrath has spread across his face.
His countenance is different, his fury strong;
If you grapple with him, my Zholoy,
Abandon hope of your precious life!
Whose name has reached Beejin,
That must be Manas, our affliction;
Of the bloodstained one who will fight us,
Those must be the gazing dark eyes!
He is no warrior to bring low and conquer;
His form is different, utterly strange,
He is no lion a mortal can defeat;
His prowess is plain.
He is no warrior to face lightly!
My dear, only yesterday,
The great lord risen above the governors,
I watched the Kakan as I passed around,
In the garden planted by the governor,
In Beejin with its forty gates,
At Karykan's throne.
Oh, my dear,
When they cut Chynmachyn's willows,
When they gathered true Beejin's people,
Its giants, mighty men and heroes,
When they gathered them all,
When they set them marching in files,
Before Karykan
I turned Chongküröng's head.
Of the seething Kytay,
I stood judging their giants.
My death had not come to take me;
In Beejin of the forty Kytay tribes,
I saw no giant like this.
His valor is extraordinary;
In the end you will see:
This bold champion will ruin the Kakan.
Manas is no ordinary lion;
He is no warrior a mortal can defeat.
If we clash, will our strength suffice?
Will he submit when we fight?
Manas, touched by Khizir,
Can a mortal bring him down?
He is a true blood-drinker.
Oh, Zholoy, can anyone who attacks survive?
He is a champion, he is a lion;
This damned Manas,
Not merely against the Kytay, as I see it,
Against the eighteen thousand worlds
Is a warrior strong enough to stand.
Yesterday our elder, our Esenkan,
Unleashed fierce wrath.
'They failed to find Manas,' he said,
And slaughtered the sorcerers.
This damned Burut
Has become the Kyrgyz people's fortress.
Now that I know his deeds,
Having all the sorcerers struck down—
That action was fitting.
Against a hero like Ala-Too,
Against an unbeliever of terrifying might,
Can a champion endure and advance?
Can one who truly fights him survive?
Those who attack him will have
Their shoulder blades smashed to powder.
That damned bloodstained one's—
Just watch, my Zholoy—
Strife will strike Beejin.
Good heavens, his fortune is complete;
He is a lion supported by holy patrons.
When I look within him,
He is wider than the earth's surface.
'He will bring strife upon Beejin,'
The seers were right to say.
For those damned Burut,
Valiant Manas, the leopard,
Is a walled city, a fortress.
When I look once, this Burut
Appears like a single man;
When I look again, this Burut
Appears like a thousand men.
Going to judge many giants,
I wore down my horse's hide;
As far as Bangbang-Sazangshang,
I traveled everywhere there was to go.
My appointed death has not taken me;
A formidable one like this
I have never seen upon the earth.
Ever since I became Ezkara,
Ever since I gained the name of seer,
I have known no such man;
I have heard of no such man.
To this slope of Altay,
I failed to come with the seers;
I have brought disaster upon myself.
My dark eyes were blinded;
I had become blind.
This Burut of a different father
Was born here in Altay.
If you live, you will see:
He will raise an uproar in Beejin.
As I examined the warrior's frame,
My collarbones began to throb,
My heart began to shake.
Strength drained from my forearms,
The covering fell from my heart.
Making the belly churn,
Here, it seems, is our distress!
The one who will lay Beejin waste,
Here, it seems, is our enemy!
Good heavens, his figure, his majesty!
Oh, my dear Zholoy, look
At his bearing on horseback!
His right shoulder is broad;
This Burut—may he be ruined!—
Is a lion who will shatter the Oyrats.
Esenkan grew wrathful
And stood in distress;
My mighty Esenkan's
Understanding was correct.
That Burut of terrifying presence,
Would he sink if cast into water?
Against Kakanchyn's Beejin,
Would he sit watching without fighting?
When he surges, he is a gray tiger.
Have you seen his form?
My Zholoy, there is no man like him!
A dark-spotted leopard
Rages at his side;
A short-tailed, gray-maned lion
Opens its mouth, preparing to strike.
If we attack, will this bloodstained one
Not wreak all the havoc he knows?
If this bloodstained one unleashes his wrath,
Will he not slaughter us all the way to the Kakan?
If he surges, he will wreak havoc;
This Burut—may his house burn!—
Of the seething Kytay,
He will seize the khanship!
His brow is high, his face fine;
His wrath is extraordinary, his fury strong.
The wise are struck with wonder;
Our heads are thrown into turmoil!
This Burut is no ordinary man;
He is no warrior who will refrain from burning.
Alas, Zholoy, open your eyes!
He seems ready to slaughter the mighty as he passes;
Destroying and slaughtering this people,
He seems ready to bring them all to ruin!
I have heard of none like him among nations;
I have seen none like him among people.
Now, Zholoy, open your eyes!
His valor is extraordinary;
His prowess is immense.
Can a man wrestle him down?
He is a lion beyond measure,
Can a man bring him low?
He is a banner raised for the Burut,
For Beejin under its Kakan,
A calamity fallen upon its head!
Thick-armed and stone-hearted,
Where has he come from,
This reckless giant with an elephant's frame?
His mace made of steel
He has raised looming high.
Clashing with countless troops,
He never opens his guard in fear.
Those who clash with him,
He crushes to earth like hares.
His brow is deep as a ravine;
This damned bloodstained one
Seems ready to swallow those who grapple.
His nose is like a massive crag;
This damned Burut
Seems ready to devour those who struggle.
Our Kytay Beejin,
If only Khizir would bless my land!
This Manas is formidable;
If only he had been born among the Kytay!
In our Kytay Beejin,
There is no equal to match him.
My idol, what am I to do?
Against this Burut devil,
There is no warrior to fight on equal terms!
If we face him, this Burut
Will drive us staggering round and round.
Zholoy, take care:
He will break your ranks apart!
He is renowned, he is a lion;
He appears unlike mortal men.
No enemy can strike his right side;
Before Manas—may he be ruined!—
Not one will remain to turn a horse-catching pole.
His companions are eighty-four chiltens;
That damned bloodstained one's
Every sweep turns the place to red fire.
If we fight, may this bloodstained one
Not descend upon our very heads,
Crushing those who attack,
May he not drink blood like water!
He is a warrior, he is a lion;
Will he spare anyone who faces him?
Let us not die in regret;
Will he ever be sated with blood in combat?
Let us think wisely and act;
Let us restrain the army without fighting.
Let us send six swift horses,
With a letter the size of a palm,
And from Kakanchyn's Beejin
Gather a great army!
Then let us swarm upon him in battle,
Summon the sorcerers,
And then capture and bind him.
Just look at Manas:
He has a black cap like a cauldron;
The whole world,
He has the will to throw into turmoil!”
